says: Then this is the last whole page, and I know what goes on it: the first window again, the one from before the sun. Same frame, same night, but with everything you taught me in it. The night solid. The lamp reflected in the glass, lifted out and then glazed back to a ghost, since you were right that a reflection is never paper white. And the cat on the sill with her back to us, grey underfur laid first with the fat point, then her stripes, which I owe her. The wall stays bare. I will not let the pencil die on a wall. It can die on a sentence.

ops.text: All the kitchens are out. The tabby has her stripes back and the best seat. Nothing out there needs drawing; she checks anyway.
